Fencing services matched to coast or hinterland The right material depends on how exposed your block is and what the fence has to do. Colorbond and aluminium slat suit the salt air and wind on the beachfront strip from Noosa Heads to Marcoola. Timber remains the right call on established hinterland streets and as a shared dividing fence. Pool fencing is its own compliance-led job wherever a barrier is involved, and rural fencing covers the paddock and acreage boundaries out through Doonan, Eumundi and Kin Kin, where different QBCC rules apply. Colorbond Fencing Steel panel boundary fencing in AU colours, built to handle coastal wind exposure from Noosa Heads to the hinterland. Timber Fencing Paling, lapped-and-capped and picket timber fencing for hinterland acreage and residential blocks. Before you commit Begin with the boundary before choosing the panel A boundary project is partly a building decision and partly a neighbour conversation. In Queensland, the Neighbourhood Disputes (Dividing Fences and Trees) Act 2011 sets a process for adjoining owners considering a sufficient dividing fence . That does not mean every premium material, extra height or preferred finish is automatically shared - an owner who wants more than sufficient covers the difference. Start with a written description of the work and at least one quote. If discussion does not settle the matter, a notice to contribute is the formal step, and the timing matters: the Act allows one month to reach agreement, followed by a possible QCAT application within two months of the notice. This is general information, not a promise about the result. Three checks before measuring Check proposed height against the ground and any retaining wall - combined height can change the approval question. A corner block can need a lower sight-line treatment so drivers can see across the intersection. A pool barrier has its own safety requirements and inspection pathway, confirmed only by a licensed pool safety inspector. If a neighbour, pool, slope or acreage boundary is involved, put that in the first enquiry so the quote starts in the right place. A metre rate is only one part of the price A rate can help you sanity-check a project, but it does not describe the whole site. Compare the inclusions below before treating two numbers as like-for-like. What you want the fence to do Privacy, airflow, street presentation and pool safety point to different materials and heights. How exposed the block is Beachfront wind and salt spray need a different post spec to a sheltered hinterland street, even at the same length. Ground conditions Coastal sand, riverfront alluvium and hinterland clay all dig and hold a post differently, which shows up in the footing spec. Access and the run itself Corners, returns, gates and hard-to-reach boundaries add time beyond the straight metres. The fence already there Removal, disposal and making good after old posts come out can be a real part of the job - ask whether it is included. Use the estimator as a starting point Add a rough length, height and working rate to see a planning range. It is a conversation starter, not a site measure or a fixed offer.
